status: Source-fit authoring design; repository acceptance, prepared classroom resources, observed attainment and staging publication remain separate.

source.review: All594 retained primary mandatory bodies and embedded examples and216 nested instructional tips read. Source-specific channels, support, topic range, variety and production conditions were compared; optional examples do not become an exhaustive grammar or product inventory.

early-oral-media.kind: Original brief French spoken invitation and information announcement; fictional classroom events
early-oral-media.invitation: Bonjour ! Demain, nous partageons des histoires dans le coin lecture. Tu peux choisir un livre de la classe. Tu peux lire, raconter ou écouter. Viens découvrir une histoire avec nous !
early-oral-media.information: La rencontre est demain, après la récréation. Les livres sont dans la boîte bleue. Nous choisissons une histoire. À la fin, nous rangeons les livres.
early-oral-media.production: A qualified French model records or speaks each text with a clear but natural voice; prepare accurate original picture/object supports. Present actual sound before any printed transcript. Make a second rendering with different deliberate emphasis, pauses or gentle background sound for a supported presentation comparison. Do not infer a universal emotional reaction.

academic-oral-media.kind: Original French project report and persuasive announcement; supplied fictional class data
academic-oral-media.report: Notre classe prépare un espace pour partager des histoires. Nous avons trois boîtes avec quatre livres dans chaque boîte : cela fait douze livres. Un groupe propose de lire ensemble près de la fenêtre. Un autre préfère un endroit calme pour lire seul. Nous pouvons garder les deux choix. La prochaine rencontre nous aidera à savoir si cet espace convient au groupe.
academic-oral-media.persuasiveVersion: Un seul choix pour notre coin lecture : tout le monde doit lire la même histoire à voix haute ! Selon cette annonce, c’est la meilleure façon de participer. Mais cette annonce ne présente pas les idées des personnes qui préfèrent écouter ou lire seules. Quelles informations manquent pour choisir une organisation qui convient au groupe ?
academic-oral-media.production: Use actual qualified spoken French, original accurate space/box/book visuals and the supplied fictional data. Some courses require unfamiliar vocabulary: select a genuinely new contextual term without preteaching that target, and check meaning from actual sound/context. Compare how choice of wording, voice and omitted perspectives changes the message; disagreement and conditional opinions are valid. No real survey findings or universal class preference is asserted.

oral-creation.kind: Actual child-created oral media tasks with checked models, not a supplied script counted as production
forms: Audio announcement or short recorded interview
Voice-over slides or illustrated spoken report
oral-creation.task: Choose a real task purpose and stated audience, plan a brief French message, record or deliver it and revise it after relevant feedback. In the second form create actual visual aids/slides: select graphics, original images or sound that clarify the main idea, explain the choice and integrate them smoothly with actual spoken French. Conduct an interview with genuine open answers or create a fresh information/invitation announcement; a written script alone does not establish oral creation. For older profiles include an academic explanation or reasoned proposal and meaningful spontaneous follow-up, rather than only a rehearsed greeting.
modelEarly: Un livre pour chacun : choisis une histoire !
Voici notre coin lecture. Les livres sont dans la boîte. Quelle histoire préfères-tu ?
modelAcademic: Voici nos deux propositions pour le coin lecture.
Trois boîtes de quatre livres donnent douze livres à partager.
Nous proposons deux espaces parce que les lecteurs ne choisissent pas tous la même activité.
oral-creation.limits: Use print-to-camera, accessible slides or equivalent tools; technology operation is not a new mastery claim. No real publication, purchases, disclosure or compulsory enthusiasm. More than a copied complete teacher sound sequence is required.

french-oral-corpus.kind: Introduced French oral vocabulary for the linked whole lexical claim
actions: lire
écouter
raconter
partager
choisir
french-oral-corpus.task: Teach actual sound/meaning/form pairs with a qualified French model and meaningful contexts. Check recognition and meaningful independent French recall of nouns, actions and feelings after study and a delay, then use them in changed familiar scenes. Do not infer lexical mastery from echoing, an English result or a previously checked different French corpus. The delay is a whole-claim check, not a publisher minimum.

poster-comparison.kind: Two original classroom media layouts to prepare and read in French

versionA.heading: Viens partager une histoire !
versionA.body:
Demain, après la récréation
Coin lecture
Tu peux lire, raconter ou écouter.
versionA.layout: Readable large invitation title; original book-group image; distinct time/place block; visible participation choices.

versionB.heading: Une seule bonne façon de lire ?
versionB.body:
Lis la même histoire à voix haute.
Tout le monde va adorer !
versionB.layout: Oversized command and promise; tiny or missing alternative-choice information; contrasting colour and framing. This is a fictional message for critique, not a recommendation.

poster-comparison.task: Prepare both actual posters and compare the message, audience and how specific words, size, colour, layout and perspective affect the learner’s interpretation. Give a supported opinion using an actual feature as evidence. No required positive feeling or universal claim about how all audiences respond.

graphic-story.kind: Original three-panel French comic/illustrated scene; visual preparation is required

panels.drawing: Lina holds an empty book bag beside a shelf; a blue book lies under the nearby chair.
A peer points towards the chair; the book remains visible below it.
Lina and the peer hold the blue book; its cover shows a garden.

graphic-story.task: Prepare actual original panels with readable captions and deliberate framing/colour. Explain how the pictures advance the search and add the book’s location and cover detail beyond the captions. Compare the scene presented as plain written captions, as the illustrated sequence and as a qualified spoken French account; explain what changes in meaning/tone or available clues. Invite a supported alternative interpretation. Retain the whole prior French picture/text protocol; a logo or one word/picture match is insufficient.

word-meaning-references.kind: Original checked French context, picture-reference and synonym entries; use several actual resources
word-meaning-references.context: La pluie commence. Lina entre dans la petite cabane. Cet abri la protège de la pluie.
word-meaning-references.picturePreparation: Prepare an original picture of Lina in the roofed shelter and rain outside, plus a separately labelled word/picture reference. A picture description alone is not a visual meaning check.

entries.abri: Ici, un lieu qui protège de la pluie.

word-meaning-references.task: Encounter a genuinely unfamiliar target in connected print, ask and answer a meaning question, infer from actual context/picture clues and confirm with an actual checked French reference. Explain a link with a known word or idea, then apply it in a changed context. Compare the reference, a personal word/picture bank and the connected passage when reviewing word choice. If all supplied targets are familiar, prepare and verify another contextual target; an unverified dictionary label is insufficient. Keep actually used reference entries available for checking.

word-choice-scenes.kind: Original French written comparisons and word-bank choices
word-choice-scenes.vague: Le lapin va à la maison. Son grand chapeau tombe sur son nez.
word-choice-scenes.preciseHumorous: Le petit lapin bondit vers la maison. Son énorme chapeau glisse sur son nez.
word-choice-scenes.task: Write a plain and a deliberately humorous or suspenseful version of the same scene, replace vague wording with precise choices and explain the intended effect. Choose an effective verb AND adjective from the bank for a stated scene and justify both; do not reward a random longer word. The learner creates fresh alternatives and checks actual French meaning, not merely copies these models. No compulsory laughter, decorative adjective quota or oral dialogue-rehearsal prerequisite.

own-voice.kind: Original short French opinion models; change purpose/content rather than copy
own-voice.early: Je préfère écouter une histoire dans le coin lecture parce que j’aime imaginer les personnages. Et toi, que préfères-tu ?
own-voice.academic: À mon avis, notre espace doit proposer plusieurs façons de participer. Certaines personnes souhaitent lire seules, et d’autres veulent raconter une histoire. Deux choix nous permettent de partager les livres sans imposer la même activité à tous.
own-voice.task: Create an original supported French opinion about a book, topic or class proposal, name the subject, state a clear personal view with a reason and make deliberate vocabulary/style choices suited to its reader. Compare a plain and an intended-effect version and explain how the wording expresses that view. In beginning profiles use teacher support and brief familiar sentences; in later profiles develop an academic or personally relevant viewpoint with coherent supporting details. A supplied “je pense” copied without a clear own message is insufficient.

multimodal-production.kind: Three actual writing-plus-visual products, preserving the whole existing claim

informativeModel.title: Notre coin lecture
informativeModel.paragraph: Le coin lecture est un espace pour découvrir des livres et partager des histoires. Les livres de la classe sont rangés dans une boîte. On peut lire, raconter ou écouter une histoire. Cet espace permet de choisir une activité de lecture avec le groupe.
informativeModel.diagramPreparation: Prepare an original labelled diagram showing the book box and two activity areas. Add a caption explaining the arrangement; the learner makes or meaningfully adapts the actual diagram.

persuasiveModel.heading: Choisis une histoire !
persuasiveModel.body: Un livre de la classe suffit. Tu peux lire, raconter ou écouter.
persuasiveModel.task: Create the actual digital or equivalent poster; choose images, readable font size and layout for its stated invitation audience and explain those choices.

pictureBookModel.illustrationPreparation: Prepare an original picture adding a visible blue book under the chair and a cover detail not in the text. Learner-created or meaningfully adapted visuals must add compatible information rather than decorate the caption.
pictureBookModel.task: Publish a fresh picture-book page with French text and an illustration that adds meaning, then edit BOTH modes after feedback.

multimodal-production.process: Plan purpose/reader and content; compose actual French writing and visuals; revise content and both modes after feedback, proofread and prepare a finished classroom copy. The informative piece includes a clear topic, facts/definition, concrete detail and a concluding statement; independently preserve the retained Basic Informational Writing readiness claim. Preserve all earlier whole process, sentence, feedback and sustained-writing readiness checks separately. A voice-only recording, copied template or headings without actual writing/visual work is insufficient. No full multi-paragraph organisation claim is inferred from one short paragraph.

french-conventions.kind: Original fictional editing examples and fresh learner production, not fabricated learner errors
french-conventions.complete: Les élèves lisent dans le coin lecture.
french-conventions.expanded: Les élèves lisent une histoire près de la fenêtre pendant la rencontre.
french-conventions.wordOrderDraft: Les livres dans la boîte sont.
french-conventions.wordOrderRevision: Les livres sont dans la boîte.
french-conventions.timeDraft: Hier, nous rangeons les livres, puis nous avons fermé la boîte.
french-conventions.timeRevision: Hier, nous avons rangé les livres, puis nous avons fermé la boîte.
french-conventions.connectedModel: Voici les livres que nous avons choisis. Nous les rangeons dans la boîte parce que la rencontre est terminée.
french-conventions.task: Distinguish a fragment from a complete French thought; construct complete subject/verb sentences in speech and writing and expand one meaningfully. Use the fictional examples to inspect actual word order, noun/adjective agreement, familiar spelling/accents, punctuation and intended time, then create and proofread fresh connected French work and obtain teacher/peer feedback. Correct a supplied tense mismatch, explain the intended time, revise a real aspect of the fresh writing after feedback and reread for clarity. Qualified French checking selects appropriate parts of speech and conventions for the course context, including connected sentences and questions, rather than treats the models as a complete grammar inventory. Copied corrections alone or an old English editing result do not certify French application.

actions: Before three different actual French listening tasks, identify why the learner is listening: carry out ordered directions, gather the main message/details or respond to another viewpoint. Explain what information matters and how the response will show understanding; the same text can support a different stated purpose.

Keep the whole simple planning claim: describe task and sequence, independently divide a larger supported listening-and-response task into manageable steps, and gather the needed information or materials before starting. After the task check whether the response fits its purpose; that checks the retained self-checking readiness rather than automatically certifying it.

Use the bound earlier four-step French instruction/clarification task and the actual oral media resources. Do not infer listening-purpose awareness merely from successful imitation or a generic stated learning goal.
nearMiss: Only says listen carefully, with no purpose or relevant information.
Copies a prepared plan without deciding task, order or resources.
listening-purpose.transfer: Change from following directions to gathering information or comparing a viewpoint and adapt the actual plan.

actions: Hear at least the actual spoken invitation/information and a differently presented version, with the course support. Give an actual verbal response AND an original non-verbal response (drawing, role play or another accessible representation) about the message and how it was presented.

State a view and explain its reason, participate in an actual supported discussion/presentation and explain thinking. Meaningful supported participation fulfils the confidence evidence; no facial expression, compulsory enthusiasm or personality rating.

In later profiles explain the reaction with an actual word, voice, sound or presentation feature as evidence. Do not replace actual heard French with reading an English transcript. Teacher support remains available; opinions may differ.
nearMiss: Only identifies a word or says like/dislike without a message/presentation account.
Supplies only a verbal response when both channels are required.
oral-media-response.transfer: Change the voice, framing or intended audience and justify a supported reaction.

actions: Produce the two actual oral-media forms in oral-creation, using the selected course repertoire/purpose/audience. Prepare and integrate real visuals and actual spoken French rather than score a written script or teacher echo.

Keep the full multimedia claim: select a meaningful visual/image/sound, create actual visual aids that clarify main ideas and integrate them smoothly with the presentation. Explain the choices and revise a choice after feedback.

Complete the whole introduced French lexical recognition, delayed independent meaningful retrieval and changed-scene use in french-oral-corpus. Neither the old English operation nor a different French word list certifies the actual corpus.
nearMiss: A decorative slide without actual oral performance.
One copied announcement counted as independent creation or lexical retention.
oral-media-creation.transfer: Change purpose/audience and recombine familiar French language and media choices.

actions: Read actual French posters and the prepared graphic story. Give a supported personal response to the messages AND their presentation, including text/visual evidence for later profiles. Explain author choices of words, structure, tone and perspective and their actual effect on the reader; the desired effect may not match the reader’s response.

Complete the full multimedia operation: explain how comic pictures advance the scene or convey a supported mood; analyse colour/layout effects; compare the same scene in written, illustrated and spoken forms. Preserve the whole prior picture/text operation using the original French story and actual compatible illustrations, not only a logo.

State an opinion with a reason and explain thinking in a real supported discussion/presentation. Reading remains the learner interpreting French print; an adult reading or translating the complete text cannot stand for it.
nearMiss: A French word/picture match counted as full visual/media analysis.
Names a colour without its contribution to the message.
reading-media-response.transfer: Change one framing/layout/word choice and compare the supported interpretation.

actions: Use the actual contextual passage, prepared picture/reference, personal bank and word bank to confirm meaning, review, refine and vary actual French choices. Ask/answer a new-word question, infer using context/picture and explain a connection to a known word or idea. Several resources must actually be used, not merely named.

Keep the whole vivid-choice operation: write plain and purposeful humorous/suspenseful versions, replace vague wording with precise alternatives and explain the effect, and justify both a chosen verb and adjective for a stated context. No new lower-demand French clone or compulsory oral sentence rehearsal.
nearMiss: A dictionary named but no entry or meaning check used.
Changes a word without knowing its meaning or intended effect.
word-meaning-and-choice.transfer: Use a verified new contextual term and a changed scene, checking actual French meaning again.

actions: Write an original French opinion piece that names its topic/book, makes a clear own choice or view and gives a reason. Make deliberate word/style choices suited to the intended reader; in early courses use the stated teacher support and familiar repertoire.

Retain the full vivid-word comparison, intended-effect explanation and justified verb/adjective choices. A copied first-person phrase or teacher’s view with a changed name does not establish personal voice. Later profiles use connected personally relevant or academic ideas and suitable supporting details.
nearMiss: Copies je pense with no clear own message.
Calls every long word better without explaining its intended effect.
voice-and-viewpoint.transfer: Express a changed view for a different reader while preserving clear meaning and deliberate choices.

actions: Plan, create, edit and publish the actual informative writing+diagram/caption, purposeful poster and fresh picture-book page from multimodal-production. Use more than one simple media form in early courses and a suitable variety of forms/techniques for later course contexts.

Choose actual graphics, layout and font sizes for purpose/audience and explain how they support the written message. Ensure the picture-book illustration adds compatible meaning beyond the words, then revise BOTH writing and image after feedback.

Keep the full informative topic/facts/definition/conclusion and separate original writing/readiness checks; do not infer extended paragraph-organisation mastery from a one-paragraph work. Actual French composition and taught-form checking are required; an old English artefact, audio-only item or copied final model is insufficient.
nearMiss: Poster has only headings or copied words and no actual learner writing/visual decisions.
Changes decoration while omitting meaningful revision of both modes.
written-media-creation.transfer: Make another media form for a changed purpose/audience with fresh French writing and justified visual choices.

actions: For Immersion4–6 only, perform the full actual French fragment/complete thought, sentence generation/expansion and fresh proofreading/revision tasks in french-conventions. Check appropriate word classes, word order, familiar spelling/accents and punctuation in meaningful connected text and questions.

Retain actual tense consistency, teacher/peer content feedback and a reasoned revision followed by rereading. Source examples guide the course complexity without becoming a complete universal grammar inventory. A generic sentence/editing result in English, or copying fictional corrected strings without producing/editing fresh French work, is insufficient.
nearMiss: Identifies a subject but does not create a complete French sentence.
Corrects only a supplied accent and omits word order, grammar, time, punctuation or fresh revision.
french-sentence-conventions.transfer: Change the subject, time and intended message and check the appropriate actual conventions again.

dependencyReview.status: Two intrinsically justified hard-to-soft corrections proposed alongside complete whole-target source tasks. No learner-state change.
dependencyReview.sourceMotivation: Actual Extended/Immersion sources require media production and word-choice/voice operations. Do not mint French/easier clones or soften gates solely to fit a source; these two counterexamples apply to the entire unchanged English target too.

before.reason: Choosing words for effect builds on oral rehearsal and vocabulary building

after.reason: Orally rehearsing varied sentence structures can support word choice, but deliberately choosing precise and vivid words and phrases in writing does not require first rehearsing dialogue or varied sentence openings aloud. Preserve the complete written comparison, intended effect and justified verb/adjective choices.

wholeTarget.subject: English
wholeTarget.name: Vivid Word Choices
wholeTarget.description: Choose precise and vivid words and phrases to create specific effects in writing
evidence: Replace vague words in 'The nice man went to the big house' with more precise alternatives and explain the effect
Write two versions of the same scene — one with plain language and one with carefully chosen words for suspense or humour
Select from a word bank the most effective verb and adjective for a given sentence, justifying each choice
wholeTarget.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes descriptive or creative pieces, do they choose interesting and precise words — like "sprinted" instead of "ran", or "crimson" instead of "red" — to create a specific effect?

wholePrerequisite.subject: English
wholePrerequisite.name: Rehearsing and Varying Sentences
wholePrerequisite.description: Compose and rehearse sentences orally before writing, progressively building varied and rich vocabulary and an increasing range of sentence structures including dialogue
evidence: Rehearse a sentence containing dialogue aloud before writing it (e.g. 'Let's go!' shouted Tom)
Orally compose sentences with varied openers (e.g. time adverbials, subordinate clauses) before writing
Try out two or three different ways to express the same idea orally and choose the most effective version to write
wholePrerequisite.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} try out a sentence aloud before writing it — experimenting with different words and structures to find the version that sounds best?

changes.hypotheticalIndependentEnglishWitness: Hypothetical whole-target English witness: independently replace vague wording with precise alternatives and explain the effect; write a plain and a deliberately humorous version of the same scene; choose an effective verb and adjective from a bank and justify both. The writer works directly in writing and has not demonstrated the separate oral rehearsal of dialogue or varied sentence openings. All target evidence remains; oral performance is not silently added to it.

before.reason: 'Making multimodal texts' builds on 'Organising Writing into Paragraphs'

after.reason: Paragraph organisation can support extended multimodal writing, but planning, creating, editing and publishing writing with purposeful visuals can be demonstrated in a single-page or short-caption work without organising an extended text into several themed paragraphs. Keep the full writing-plus-image, informative paragraph, diagram/caption, audience/layout and revision requirements.

wholeTarget.subject: English
wholeTarget.name: Making multimodal texts
wholeTarget.description: Plan, create, edit and publish multimodal texts that combine writing with visual features — images, labelled diagrams, captions, headings and layout — using digital or print tools, choosing visual features to suit the purpose and audience
evidence: Create a digital slide, poster or e-book page that combines a short informative paragraph with a labelled diagram and a caption
Choose images, font sizes and layout in a digital tool to suit a persuasive purpose (e.g. a poster for the school fete) and explain the choices
Publish a picture-book page where the illustration adds meaning not stated in the text, then edit both text and image after feedback
wholeTarget.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} make a poster or slide that combines writing with pictures, labels and captions — choosing a layout that suits what it's for?

wholePrerequisite.subject: English
wholePrerequisite.name: Organising Writing into Paragraphs
wholePrerequisite.description: Organise writing into paragraphs, grouping related material around a theme, and use simple organisational devices such as headings and sub-headings in non-narrative writing
evidence: Divide a piece of writing into paragraphs, each focused on one main idea or aspect of the topic
Use headings and sub-headings to organise a non-fiction text (e.g., a report about animals with sections 'Habitat', 'Diet', 'Appearance')
Identify where a new paragraph should begin in a given text and explain why (e.g., 'A new paragraph starts here because the topic changes from appearance to diet')
wholePrerequisite.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a longer piece — like a report or a story — do they organise it into paragraphs, with related ideas grouped together and, where appropriate, headings to help the reader navigate?

changes.hypotheticalIndependentEnglishWitness: Hypothetical whole-target English witness: create a page with a short informative paragraph, labelled diagram and caption; choose images, font size and layout for a persuasive poster and explain the audience choices; publish and revise a picture-book page whose illustration adds meaning beyond the text, editing both modes after feedback. These complete products do not establish the separate ability to divide an extended text into thematic paragraphs and justify paragraph breaks. This is not an audio-only or template-copying shortcut.

retainedHardRequirements: Makingmultimodaltexts→BasicInformationalWriting remains hard and full facts/definitions/concluding statement are explicitly checked separately.
Existing paragraph, stamina, sentence-rehearsal and process-vocabulary claims are not narrowed or removed.
All other existing edges and authored cards/guides remain exact.
rejectedBroaderMatches: VocabularyStrategies includes Greek/Latin roots and multiple-meaning word work; it is not silently reduced into a primary word-wall task. Existing DiscussingandQuestioningNewWords covers the required actual context/picture/word-link questions with source-specific reference resources.
SupportingIdeasWithEvidence requires evaluating author argument support; a personal response backed by one media feature alone does not establish its whole claim.
WritingTechniquesForEffect requires broader literary/rhetorical application; beginning a personal voice is not a new easier version of that node.
dependencyReview.freshSourceMeaning: All594 mandatory source bodies/examples and216 nestedtips read, with originalEnglishPDF discrepancy reconciliation.

wholeClaimBoundaries: All existing authored cards, guides and scoped intervals remain unchanged; context-derived flat envelopes may widen only from actual primary source intervals. No new French/grade/media clone.
Source fit is not learner mastery or automatic English-to-French transfer. Prepare actual checked French sound/print/visual resources and collect fresh performance in the actual corpus.
All unmodified hard prerequisites remain separate whole readiness requirements. No unrelated graph, paragraph or Greek/Latin-root tasks are invented solely to certify these source duties.
This slice selects66 exact records only. The other396 Extended/Immersion records remain under task qualification, including local-community applicability; no whole-programme completion claim.
Original French texts are fictional teaching designs, not official quotations, authentic community testimony, proven intervention results or real class data.
